concept.title: Content hierarchy
concept.shortdesc: refers to how information is logically organized across topics based on user intent and information

conbody.p: Content hierarchy refers to how information is logically organized across topics based on user intent and information type. DITA enforces this through its topic types such as concept, task, and reference, which naturally create a layered understanding.

A typical content hierarchy follows this progression:
Concept topic: Explains what a feature is and why it matters
Task topic: Shows how to use the feature
Reference topic: Provides detailed specifications
Troubleshooting topic: Addresses common problems
Glossary topic: Defines unfamiliar terms and standardizes terminology
